title: From $18M Draft to $5.5M Closing: The Black Family Partners Repricing
scope: Forensic-accounting reconstruction of Financial Trust Company's 2012 three-asset sale package to Black Family Partners, including aggregate repricing, intra-package reallocation and bank settlement.

sources.supports: Oct. 31 Financial Trust 'Summary of Leon Black deals'; historical net-investment figures and compounded-return scenarios.
sources.limit: Internal model, not independent appraisal or formal tax-basis determination.

sources.supports: Unsigned Nov. 2 draft purchase-and-sale agreement with $18M aggregate and $7,793,608 / $3,496,424 / $6,709,968 asset allocations.
sources.limit: Draft contains incomplete purchaser/signature fields and does not prove an $18M closing.

sources.supports: Standalone Schedule 3.2 allocating $5.5M as $3.5M ESWW / $1M AP SHL / $1M AP Tech.
sources.limit: Provenance does not establish it as the final operative closing schedule.

sources.supports: Nov. 26 counsel transmission confirming $5.5M aggregate purchase price, Schedule 3.2 allocation and planned Nov. 30 closing.
sources.limit: Closing instruction is not by itself proof of final executed signatures.

sources.supports: Nov. 28 $5M ESWW / $250K AP SHL / $250K AP Tech allocation; 2014 later confirmation that those sales prices were used and AJE existed.
sources.limit: Does not explain why allocation changed or establish tax motive.

sources.supports: Nov. 30 $5,500,030 CHIPS credit from Black Family Partners, L.P. to Financial Trust Company.
sources.limit: Two JPM statement representations support the amount/originator; the $30 above the stated $5.5M contract price is unexplained.

sources.supports: Chronology, arithmetic reconciliation, laundering-screen negative findings and open forensic questions.
sources.limit: Archive-created synthesis; substantive claims remain tied to primary sources above.

open_questions: Why the aggregate package moved from $18M to $5.5M between Nov. 2 and Nov. 26.
Why the $5.5M allocation changed from $3.5M/$1M/$1M to $5M/$250K/$250K.
Who authored the Oct. 31 return model and selected its assumptions.
Whether the final executed purchase-and-sale agreement and signed transfer documents can be recovered.
Buyer- and seller-side 2012 tax treatment and the 2014 adjusting journal entry.
Why the Nov. 30 bank credit was $30 above the stated $5.5M purchase price.
not_established: That the $18M draft ever closed or was funded.
That the repricing/reallocation was tax-driven, valuation-driven, negotiation-driven or accounting-driven.
Money laundering, tax fraud, concealment, structuring, layering or a sham transaction.
That historical net-investment figures equal fair market value or formal tax basis.
